item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. I found a few limited positive signals, mainly rhetoric on Gaza civilians and a late-2024 refugee-law framework on paper, but the strongest operational evidence is negative: Sudanese refugees were mass-arrested and forcibly returned, refugee children were kept out of school by bureaucracy and cost barriers, and the asylum law ratified late in 2024 was widely criticized as weakening due process and protection.

- **Sisi condemns siege/starvation in Gaza and calls for protecting civilians** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | June 11, 2024 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/presidency/speeches-telegrams-posts/president-el-sisi-s-speech-at-the-urgent-humanitarian-response-for-gaza-conference/  
  Sisi described Palestinians in Gaza as innocent civilians, condemned starvation and siege, invoked international law, and called for protecting civilians and releasing hostages and detainees. This is the best direct positive evidence that he rhetorically defended a highly vulnerable population against displacement and mass harm.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.3`, `2B.7`

- **Sisi signs foreign refugees law** | Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS | December 17, 2024 | https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/sisi-signs-foreign-refugees-law/  
  The presidency said Sisi signed Law No. 164 of 2024 on the status of foreign refugees in Egypt, creating a formal legal framework and a permanent committee for refugee affairs. This is a weak positive on paper, but it is not evidence yet of effective protection in practice.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`

- **Sudan Regional Refugee Crisis: Education Cannot Wait, UNHCR, UNICEF and Strategic Partners Call for Increased Resources** | UNICEF Egypt | August 22, 2024 | https://www.unicef.org/egypt/press-releases/sudan-regional-refugee-crisis-education-cannot-wait-unhcr-unicef-and-strategic  
  The release says the Government of Egypt had taken notable steps to provide refugees with access to education services, while partners worked to expand safe, inclusive learning spaces for refugees and host-community children. The same source says needs were outpacing resources and many newly arrived children were still out of school, so this is a partial and incomplete protection signal.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.6`

- **Egypt: Authorities must end campaign of mass arrests and forced returns of Sudanese refugees** | Amnesty International | June 19, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/  
  Amnesty documented mass arrests of Sudanese refugees, including women and children, cruel detention conditions, and collective expulsions back to active conflict in Sudan without access to asylum procedures. This is strong evidence against protection of a clearly vulnerable displaced group.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`

- **World Report 2024: Egypt** | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt  
  HRW reports that Egypt’s June 2024 visa requirement made it harder for Sudanese women, children, and older people to flee conflict, creating unreasonable and potentially life-threatening delays. That is direct evidence of increased displacement risk for vulnerable people.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`

- **Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees** | Human Rights Watch | December 2, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees  
  HRW says tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children were out of school because of residency bureaucracy, costs, discrimination, and limited free public education. This is strong evidence of systematic neglect of vulnerable children rather than effective protection.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.6`, `3B.1`

- **Egypt: President al-Sisi must reject new asylum law which violates refugee rights** | Amnesty International | December 3, 2024 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/egypt-president-al-sisi-must-reject-new-asylum-law-which-violates-refugee-rights/  
  Amnesty said the new asylum law, later ratified by Sisi, restricted the right to seek asylum, lacked due process guarantees, allowed arbitrary detention and unlawful returns, and failed to protect education, housing, and social security rights. This is the clearest late-2024 evidence against a protection-oriented approach.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.1`

**Search gap**
I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a sustained Sisi-led program that directly protected internal religious, ethnic, or sectarian minorities from targeted violence inside Egypt. The most concrete evidence instead centers on Gaza civilians and Sudanese refugees, where the public rhetoric was protective but the actual refugee-management record was sharply punitive.
